Frontend spot-check (1440x900) as aarav.mehta: /ledger renders my-ledger-page + my-ledger + all 4 total cards (my-ledger-paid=₹9,440, credit=₹0, earned=₹0, earned-pending=₹0) + my-ledger-kind filter + 200 my-ledger-row-* rows each with my-ledger-view-<id> link and my-ledger-pdf-<id> button; clicking pdf button downloads INV-BUDF7366DB9.pdf (2709 bytes, valid %PDF). Clicking View navigates to /invoice/<id> which shows invoice-template='Membership invoice', invoice-number='INV-BUDF7366DB9', invoice-total=₹5,444, invoice-note with the correct membership footnote, invoice-download-pdf + invoice-print buttons both present and download button emits a real PDF. issues: Row currencies mix ₹ and $ signs because payments use their order.currency for amount, while total-paid card sums across all currencies in ₹. Not a functional bug (per-row currency is correct) but visually the summed total may not equal the sum of visible row amounts. Consider normalising per user's base currency or showing 'mixed currencies' hint.

action_items: Optional (design): /ledger total-paid card sums across mixed currencies (₹9,440) while some rows show $ amounts. Consider labelling totals as base-currency only or converting per row for display consistency.
Optional (naming): review request refers to 'CSV export' on admin Ledger tab; UI button says 'Export to Excel' (still calls the same endpoint) — clarify copy if needed.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py:7096 invoice_order authorization uses `order.get('user_id') != user['id']` — safe since user_id is always a str; but if any legacy order stored ObjectId user_id (pre-refactor rows) the equality would silently fail-open for owner match and always fall through to the finance:view branch (member sees 403 on their own order). Worth a spot check.

backend/server.py:7115 my_ledger includes payment_status in [paid, pending, failed] but sums totals['paid'] using `p['status'] == 'paid'` where status may have been overwritten to a refund_status string (line 7121). A refunded-then-paid row would drop out of the total. Consider tracking paid vs refunded separately.
backend/invoices.py:76 uses inv['seller']['name'] etc. without defensive .get — if invoice_doc ever returns a partial buyer/seller dict the PDF renderer will 500 rather than degrade gracefully.

frontend/src/components/MyLedger.jsx: downloadInvoicePdf swallows non-blob errors (axios error handler runs errMsg(e) but if responseType blob returns a JSON error body it may show '[object Blob]'; consider blob→text fallback for {detail} messages).

frontend/src/components/MyLedger.jsx line 92: uses `p.receipt || p.reference` as filename; when reference contains slashes or bad chars nothing sanitises it. Low priority (invoice_no format is safe today).
